title: A phone posts only what an allowlist names, not whatever a deny list forgot
body:
## Summary
The session route held a joined phone to a deny list (PHONE_NEVER), so nine client-postable types no phone source sends still moved or changed the TV.

## Description
TL-11 (docs/concepts/TV-LED-PAIRED-EXPERIENCE-DESIGN-2026-10-19.md:373) says the phone answers the TV's asks and does not move it. desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts refused only the listed types; view, page.ask, page.unask, lesson.set, lesson.pause, essay.type, essay.clear, essay.plan and status passed - a phone could write any status line onto the TV or clear the seated learner's paragraph off the forensic page. Registry: authorization / dispatch-chokepoint-gating (default deny) and declarative-requirements (totality). Fixed: desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:300 PHONE_MAY names the nine types a phone may post; desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:72 refuses every other type from a phone (403); desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:493 exports POSTABLE. tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs reads the phone's sources (comments stripped) and fails when they post a type the list refuses.

## Flow
- a joined phone posts {type:"status",text:"Look at the phone now"} to /api/session
- Before: 200 and the TV status line changes
- After: 403 "Only the TV moves the desk.", the session byte-identical

## Expected impact
The TV can no longer be moved or written on by a phone outside its hand-offs. A phone source that later posts a new type goes red in the derived test before it ships.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a phone posts only the types the phone sends
Before: probe on the route, a joined phone: 9 of 9 sample posts 200, 8 changed the session
After: 0 of 9, 0 changed; seeded control (task.done dropped from the list) red
Method: gate - desk-pairing-test red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: A /writing page save re-reads the learner record onto the session
body:
## Summary
The /writing page path saved an episode through saveEpisode and dispatched nothing, so the session's history and writing record stayed stale (the writing round's Lane B card, judged from the store side).

## Description
The TV path re-reads the record on writing.finished (desk/src/lib/session/store.ts REHYDRATE). desk/src/app/api/writing/finish/route.ts page path saved with no event; dispatching writing.finished there would finish a TV episode at stage coached. Fixed: a server-only event learner.reread {by} (desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:443), in REHYDRATE, moving nothing in the reducer and dropped for a learner who is not seated; not in SHAPES, so no screen or phone can post it. The finish route dispatches it after the page path's save.

## Flow
- the PC finishes an episode on /writing
- Before: learner file 1 writing line, session history 0 - the TV landing says Not started
- After: session history.at(-1) is the prompt title, the writing record keys match the file

## Expected impact
The landing and the recap show a page-path episode at once. A new REHYDRATE event reads learners.json once more per page save.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - both save paths leave the session current
Before: writing-tv-test page path: file history 1 line, session history 0
After: session history holds "Screens before bed"; writing keys equal
Method: gate - writing-tv-test red then green; desk-pairing-test NL table went red until the new type had a sample
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/writing/finish/route.ts:62 const saved = saveEpisode(who.id, step.episode); (no event before the fix)
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts REHYDRATE += "learner.reread"

title: The desk's notes on a learner rode on every session message with no reader
body:
## Summary
Session.memory was hydrated on every REHYDRATE event, written to session.json and sent in every TV and phone message, and nothing reads it.

## Description
Zero consumers: grep for `.memory` over desk/src, uat/, prototype/ and tools/*.mjs finds only the store's own hydrate lines (desk/src/lib/session/store.ts, the two rehydrate branches); the memory writer and the prompts read the learner file (desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:62). The notes are the desk's unconfirmed observations about the learner (agent-memory), sent once a second to every phone while the timer runs. Fixed: removed from Session, fresh(), both rehydrate branches and pairing.ts GUEST_BLANK; load() drops it from an older session.json.

## Flow
- a learner with a nightly note sits down
- Before: the note is on the session and in every TV and phone message
- After: absent from the session and both GETs

## Expected impact
Up to 40 notes (MEMORY_CAP) per message leave the wire. Any future reader fails tsc rather than reading a stale copy.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the notes reach only the prompts that read them
Before: note present on session, TV GET and phone GET (desk-pairing-test red)
After: absent from all three; tsc 0 (no reader)
Method: gate - desk-pairing-test red then green, tsc as the reader check
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
grep -rnE "\.memory\b" desk/src (excluding learners.ts, l.memory, jobs.memory): only store.ts:1209 and :1216 at 59b4a350^ (hydrate)
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:62 const existing = readLearner(learnerId).memory.map((n) => n.text);

title: Bound a task's name, its minutes and tonight's list, as a profile name is
body:
## Summary
task.add took any non-empty name, any finite minutes and any number of tasks from a phone, and every task rides in every message and in session.json.

## Description
Pair of PROFILE_NAME_MAX (8945f3f6): the profile name was bounded for every caller, the task name was not. desk/src/lib/session/store.ts SHAPES had task.add {name: f.name, min: f.num}. Fixed (store.ts:470): TASK_NAME_MAX 80 and whole minutes 1..180 at the door; at TASKS_MAX 20 a new task takes the place of the oldest ticked one, and with none ticked the reducer says TASKS_FULL (nothing removes a task, so a cap counting ticked ones would block the list for good).

## Flow
- a joined phone posts task.add with a 100 000-letter name and min 1e9, then 200 more adds
- Before: 200, 201 tasks, session.json 116 459 bytes
- After: 400 for the huge name; the list stops at 20; session.json 2 771 bytes

## Expected impact
Tonight's list cannot grow the session without bound. The phone AddTask input has no maxLength yet (app/phone/page.tsx, phone-surface): an 81-letter name is refused by the door.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a phone cannot grow the session through tonight's list
Before: probe: huge name 200; 201 tasks after 200 adds; session.json 116 459 bytes
After: 400; 20 tasks; 2 771 bytes
Method: gate - desk-pairing-test red then green, plus the route probe on both sides
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts (before) "task.add": { name: f.name, sub: f.subject, min: f.num }
probe: 100k-char name, min 1e9: 200 | tasks: 201 | session.json bytes: 116459 -> 400 | 20 | 2771

title: The running clock's tick rewrote session.json, photos included, every second
body:
## Summary
Every dispatch rewrote the whole session.json, and the desk's ticker dispatches timer.tick once a second while the timer runs; the file holds every page photo (data URLs).

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts dispatch called writeSession() for every event; PAGES_KEPT 8 photos of the seated learner plus every away learner's ride in the file (3.2 MB for 8 pages in the probe). Fixed: a timer.tick that does not turn the phase skips the write while the last landed write is under TICK_SAVE_MS 30 s old (store.ts:1252); a phase turn, a failed last write and every other event write at once. The module header was corrected in 935174aa.

## Flow
- start the timer on a desk with snapped pages
- Before: 60 file writes a minute, each the whole session with its photos
- After: 2 a minute; the next other event writes the clock as it stands

## Expected impact
A restart loses at most 30 s of the clock and of the evening log's minutes; nothing else waits.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer whole-session writes while the clock runs
Before: 10 ticks after timer.start: 10 writes (the file followed every tick)
After: 0 writes inside the window; focus writes at once; a phase turn writes at once
Method: gate - desk-pairing-test red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:1099 store.ticker: dispatch({ type: "timer.tick", seconds: 1 }) every 1000 ms
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts dispatch: writeSession(); (unconditional before)

title: PR2's join-delay case broke on a busy machine
body:
## Summary
desk-pairing-test PR2 asserted the right code answers under 120 ms against a 150 ms delay; with sibling suites running it went red once on an untouched tree.

## Description
tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs PR2: the undelayed join is 1.8 ms median, 10 ms max (20 joins, isolated), but contention stretched it past 120 ms in 1 of 3 loaded full-suite runs this round. Fixed: delay 1000 ms, refusal >= 900 ms, right code < 900 ms; seeded control (joinDelay resolving at once) red.

## Flow
- run the desk gate while other suites run
- Before: "the right code is not delayed" red with no defect
- After: green in 3 full runs and 6 isolated runs

## Expected impact
The desk gate stops showing a red no change caused. The suite runs ~1.7 s longer.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the case fails only on a defect
Before: 1 red in 3 loaded full-suite runs; margin 120 ms
After: 0 in 3 full and 6 isolated runs; margin 900 ms; seeded control red
Method: gate - repeated runs and a seeded control
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs:306 (before) assert(Date.now()-t0<120,'the right code is not delayed') with DESK_JOIN_DELAY_MS 150
probe: right-code join ms: median 1.8 max 10.1

title: matchPiece read each kept piece twice
body:
## Summary
matchPiece walked listPieces (which reads every piece file) and then read each candidate again with getPiece.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/texts.ts matchPiece runs on every Essay keep that names no piece (desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:182), over up to 50 pieces of up to 100 KB a version. Fixed: allPieces (texts.ts:106) reads each piece once, most recent first; listPieces maps it and matchPiece compares the piece it holds.

## Flow
- keep an essay with no piece named on a shelf of 10
- Before: 20 reads for a no-match, 15 for a heading match after 5 newer pieces
- After: 10 each

## Expected impact
Half the file reads per keep on a full shelf. Same order, same result.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one read per piece per match
Before: texts-rules-test, 10 pieces, a no-match and a heading match: 35 piece-file reads
After: 20
Method: gate - texts-rules-test red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: session-link-test's reset pin was satisfied by the declaration
body:
## Summary
TL-4's "the backoff resets on a message" pin matched `attempt = 0` anywhere in raw source, and the declaration satisfies it alone.

## Description
tools/session-link-test.cjs asserted /attempt = 0/ over desk/src/tv/useSession.ts; the declaration at desk/src/tv/useSession.ts:19 matches, so taking the reset out of onmessage (desk/src/tv/useSession.ts:31) stayed green - a link that dropped once would back off at the 30 s cap all evening. The suite also matched raw text (comments count). Fixed: comments stripped before every pin; the reset pinned as onmessage's own; the case carries its seeded control.

## Flow
- remove `attempt = 0;` from the onmessage handler
- Before: the suite stays green
- After: red

## Expected impact
The backoff reset is actually pinned. Test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the pin fails on the defect it names
Before: probe on the seeded source: old pin true (green over the defect)
After: new pin false (red); both true on the real source
Method: gate - seeded control inside the case
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/tv/useSession.ts:19 let es: EventSource | null = null, dead = false, attempt = 0;
tools/session-link-test.cjs (before) assert.match(t,/attempt = 0/);

title: Every tick sends the whole session, photos included, to every stream
instrument: probe-b1 (bytes of view(s,"phone") with 8 snapped pages) on both arms, plus a TV render test that a page image is drawn from a by-reference URL; seeded: an img put back on the session must go red
body:
## Summary
While the timer runs, the ticker dispatches once a second and every TV and phone stream gets the full session; 99.9% of a message with 8 pages is the page photos.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/session/stream/route.ts sends JSON.stringify(view(s)) on every dispatch; desk/src/lib/session/store.ts Page.img holds the snapped photo as a data URL (1280 px JPEG from desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:256). Registry: realtime-events / coalescing-and-batching and push-vs-refetch-reconciliation: a blob that does not change should travel by reference, not with every tick. Fix shape: pages carry an image URL (/api/page/<id>/img, role-checked), the session holds the bytes only on disk; the TV (desk/src/tv, tv-surface) draws from the URL. Out of this round's paths and an in-tree wire contract without a verifier, so Lane B.

## Flow
- snap 8 pages, start the timer
- each second: 3.2 MB to each TV and phone stream, 192 MB a minute per stream
- a Fire TV Stick parses 3.2 MB of JSON a second

## Expected impact
The phone's Wi-Fi and battery and the Stick's main thread stop carrying the photos every second. Risk: every screen that draws a page image moves to the URL.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - per-tick messages without photos
Before: probe: message 3 202 314 bytes, photos 3 200 184 (99.9%), 192 MB a minute per stream
After: predicted ~2 KB a message
Method: probe - Before measured; the After needs the TV render seam (tv-surface)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe-b1: pages 8 message bytes 3202314 of which photos 3200184 (99.9%) | per minute of running clock per stream 192 MB
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:1099 dispatch({ type: "timer.tick", seconds: 1 }) every second

title: Every learners.json write reads and parses the file twice
instrument: learners-save-test: count readFileSync calls on learners.json per recordAttempt, recordWriting, addHistory, addDigest, addPaper and addHints (2 each today); seeded: a writer that skips the unreadable-file guard must fail the WD14 cases
body:
## Summary
getLearner reads and parses learners.json, then saveLearner -> writeLearner reads and parses it again before writing; saveEnglish was fixed to read once (fe3bd2b2), its six siblings were not.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:311 getLearner -> readAll; :186 writeLearner -> readBook again. recordAttempt (:364), recordWriting (:390), addHistory (:420), addDigest (:435), addPaper (:480) and addHints (:458, readLearner + saveLearner) all pay two reads and two parses of the whole book (every learner) per write; saveEnglish (:342) reads once. Fix shape: one updateLearner(id, f) that reads the book once, keeps the unreadable-file refusal, applies f and writes. M across one file plus the callers that use saveLearner(withX(getLearner(...))) in lib/desk and lib/english.

## Flow
- mark a set: recordAttempt per item
- each item: two whole-book reads and parses, one write
- after: one read, one write

## Expected impact
Half the learners.json I/O on every write. Risk: the unreadable-file guard (WD13/WD14) lives in the second read; the helper must keep it.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one read per learner write
Before: walked: 2 reads per write at 6 sites (saveEnglish: 1)
After: predicted 1
Method: simulation - read the six paths; the counting instrument is not built
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A stalled stream may queue 32 whole-session messages, ~100 MB, before it is let go
instrument: desk-pairing-test PR6 variant on a session with 8 photo pages: queued bytes on an unread phone stream before it closes (Before ~32 x 3.2 MB); a size-aware strategy (each chunk max(1, bytes/512 KB) units, highWaterMark 32) on the other arm; seeded: the count strategy back must go red
body:
## Summary
The stream's queue is counted in messages (CountQueuingStrategy, UNREAD 32), not bytes, and a message is 3.2 MB with 8 pages.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/session/stream/route.ts:25 UNREAD = 32 and :64 new CountQueuingStrategy({ highWaterMark: UNREAD }). A sleeping phone with the timer running holds up to 32 x 3.2 MB in server memory per stream for ~32 s; each device keeps 4 streams (DEVICE_STREAMS) and the desk lists 8 phones. Fix shape: a size function so the cap is ~16 MB or 32 small messages. Lane B: a closed stream reopens and is sent the whole session again, so the right cap needs an A/B on a real slow link.

## Flow
- a phone sleeps with the timer running on a desk with 8 pages
- its stream queues one 3.2 MB message a second
- it is let go after 32: ~102 MB held

## Expected impact
Bounded server memory per stalled stream. Risk: a slow phone is let go sooner and reconnects.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - queued bytes per stalled stream are bounded
Before: walked: 32 x 3 202 314 bytes (probe-b1 message size) = ~102 MB
After: predicted <= 16 MB
Method: simulation - arithmetic on the measured message size; the instrument is not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/session/stream/route.ts:25 const UNREAD = 32;
desk/src/app/api/session/stream/route.ts:64 }, new CountQueuingStrategy({ highWaterMark: UNREAD }));

title: The session store imports five TV view modules that import it back
instrument: a desk-boundaries rule: nothing under desk/src/lib/session imports desk/src/tv (seeded red at 5 today, green after the constants move to lib/rules)
body:
## Summary
store.ts, the only state, imports constants from tv/profileRows, tv/sheetRows, tv/landingRows, tv/mathsRows and tv/keys, and each of those imports store.ts: five import cycles between the state and the TV view layer.

## Description
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:16-20 import AGE_RANGE, NAME_FIRST, SYSTEMS, yearRange, firstToLook, LANDING_REST, dayOf and focusAfterRewrite; tv/keys.ts (798 lines, the D-pad handler) is pulled into every server route that imports the store. These are decisions (age ranges, the day, the first item to look at) and belong in desk/src/lib/rules, which the TV imports. tools/desk-boundaries.cjs does not check the direction. Out of this round's paths (the tv files are tv-surface's), so Lane B.

## Flow
- grep "@/tv" desk/src/lib/session/store.ts: 5 imports
- grep "lib/session/store" in each: 1 each
- move the eight constants to lib/rules, add the boundaries rule

## Expected impact
The state module stops depending on the screens that render it; a TV refactor can no longer change the reducer. Risk: eight constants move, every importer follows.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the state module depends on rules, not on views
Before: probe: 5 imports from desk/src/tv in store.ts, 5 cycles
After: predicted 0, pinned by a boundaries rule
Method: probe - grep both directions; the move is another context's files
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A crash on the unjoined phone never reaches the server log
body:
## Summary
app/global-error.tsx reports a crashed screen to /api/fault, but the proxy answers a guest 401 for every route but the session's, so a phone that has not joined yet - the first screen a new phone sees - reports nothing.

## Description
desk/src/proxy.ts:15 OPEN lists only /api/session and its stream; desk/src/app/global-error.tsx:13 posts /api/fault; desk/src/app/api/fault/route.ts logs short sanitised labels only (\w/.:- , 80/40 chars) and answers 204. Opening POST /api/fault to a guest widens what anyone on the network may reach (a log line per request), so it is a policy-loosen: the operator decides. A rate bound (one line per label per minute) would be the condition.

## Flow
- a phone opens /phone, has not joined, and a render throws
- global-error posts /api/fault
- the proxy answers 401; the operator never learns of it

## Expected impact
The operator sees pre-join crashes. Risk: a guest can write sanitised lines to the server log.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - pre-join crash reports reach the log
Before: probe (read): guest POST /api/fault -> 401 by OPEN
After: 204 and one line, if the operator opens it
Method: probe - the proxy table read; building it is a policy-loosen
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence:
desk/src/proxy.ts:15 const OPEN: Record<string, string[]> = { "/api/session": ["GET", "POST"], "/api/session/stream": ["GET"] };
desk/src/app/global-error.tsx:13 fetch("/api/fault", { method: "POST", ... })
